cells.tense: You are reading what is starting and walking into it awake, right now.
cells.ask: Keep one thing on your bench that isn't finished yet — let it live half-made for another week.
cells.core:
You're taking in what's half-formed and enjoying it. Someone gets excited about an idea in front of you and you don't rush to fix it or file it — you stay with it, see where it wants to go, and follow it a few steps further than the room expected. That's the whole thing working. What you sense is new and you just keep engaging it, so it stays new.

Because of that, when you say what you've been seeing, it comes out with a future in it. Your sense of what's next isn't a guess you defend — it's the shape the thing has been asking for, and people can feel the difference. Keep feeding it at the rate you've been feeding it, no harder. It's a moving thing, and it doesn't need to arrive anywhere today.
cells.sheetLine: You take in what isn't finished, and that's the use of you.
cells.verb: sensing and imagining, navigation by fresh wonder
cells.place: the place where what you already are is finally allowed to show

cells.tense: Ahead of everything, you're already braced for a future you'll never get to write in.
cells.ask: Doodle the thing you fear in one minute, then keep the doodle. Cost is a minute and being wrong in ink.
cells.core:
You're out past the end of what you actually know. Every not-yet becomes a scene you can already feel, and you keep rehearsing it before it's happened — so you're answering things nobody said and preparing for rooms that aren't there yet. The imaginer is still running. It's just stopped taking in anything new, because the pictures already occupy all the space.

So the fix wasn't in the pictures.

The way out isn't to stop imagining — it's to get interested in something small that's actually here. Sketch the fear, or put your hands on something material and tend it, and let the picture follow that instead of leading. Do one of those today and check the other one after. The dread was only ever the version ahead of the fact.
cells.sheetLine: You're dreaming ahead of what has actually happened.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door the rest of you already walked through.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about what you noticed today, to one person, in a sentence. No explanation owed.
cells.core:
There's something you felt coming, and the offering of it has gone quiet. The perceiving is still fine — it's the saying that stopped. You hold a sense of a room or a person so directly that it doesn't need argument, and not saying it out loud starts to look like not knowing it.

So take one small reading you already have — that sense of what's underneath the ordinary sentence — and say it once. Listen for what comes back. Someone else's plain reaction is the thing that lets your own knowing land, and you don't have to prove any of it before you speak.

cells.tense: You have been running the thing without owning the claim, in a room you are already writing.
cells.ask: Choose one practice you've been calling your life's, and write your name on it in a sentence today.
cells.core:
The way a first meeting gets handled, the half-second before you answer, the thing that pulls someone toward the version of you they didn't expect — that's your resonance, already on the road. What hasn't happened is the credit-taking. You call it instinct, or the moment, or just how it went, and leave your own hand out of it.

Pick one deliberately made thing — a practice, a ritual, a rule you follow because it's yours — and put your name on it in plain words. Sit with it seated. The running keeps going either way, and it works better when it's yours on purpose.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering this already. You just haven't signed it.
